woundTypes.name: Stage I Pressure Injury
woundTypes.description: Non-blanchable erythema of intact skin. Skin may be painful, firm, soft, warmer, or cooler than adjacent tissue.

woundTypes.name: Stage II Pressure Injury
woundTypes.description: Partial thickness skin loss with exposed dermis. Shallow open ulcer with pink/red wound bed. May present as intact or ruptured serum-filled blister.
assessmentPoints: Measure length x width x depth

woundTypes.name: Stage III Pressure Injury
woundTypes.description: Full thickness skin loss. Subcutaneous fat visible. May have slough, undermining, tunneling. Depth varies by body location.
assessmentPoints: Measure length x width x depth
Assess wound edges and periwound skin

woundTypes.name: Stage IV Pressure Injury
woundTypes.description: Full thickness tissue loss with exposed or palpable fascia, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage, or bone. Slough or eschar may be present.

woundTypes.name: Deep Tissue Pressure Injury
woundTypes.description: Intact or non-intact skin with localized area of persistent non-blanchable deep red, maroon, or purple discoloration, or epidermal separation revealing a dark wound bed or blood-filled blister.

woundTypes.name: Surgical Incision
woundTypes.description: Post-surgical wound typically closed with staples, sutures, or steri-strips. Assessed for healing, signs of infection, dehiscence.
assessmentPoints: REEDA scale: Redness, Edema, Ecchymosis, Discharge, Approximation
Monitor for signs of infection (warmth, erythema spreading, purulent drainage, fever)
dressingOptions: VAC if dehisced with heavy drainage

woundTypes.name: Wound Dehiscence
woundTypes.description: Separation of a surgical wound at the incision line. Ranges from superficial skin separation to evisceration (organ protrusion). Medical emergency if evisceration occurs.
assessmentPoints: Assess depth — superficial vs through fascia
dressingOptions: Evisceration: cover with sterile saline-soaked gauze — CALL PROVIDER IMMEDIATELY

woundTypes.name: Diabetic Foot Ulcer
woundTypes.description: Wound on the foot of a diabetic patient, typically due to neuropathy, poor circulation, or pressure. High infection and amputation risk.
assessmentPoints: Check for signs of osteomyelitis (probe-to-bone test)
dressingOptions: Offloading is priority (total contact cast, DH walker)

woundTypes.name: Venous Leg Ulcer
woundTypes.description: Wound typically on medial lower leg due to chronic venous insufficiency and venous hypertension. Associated with edema, lipodermatosclerosis, varicosities.
assessmentPoints: Ankle-brachial index (ABI) before compression — ABI > 0.8 required for compression
dressingOptions: Compression therapy is cornerstone — multilayer compression bandage

woundTypes.name: Arterial Ulcer
woundTypes.description: Wound due to arterial insufficiency and ischemia. Typically on toes, heels, or bony prominences. Punched-out appearance, pale wound bed, minimal drainage.
assessmentPoints: ABI assessment — ABI < 0.5 indicates severe ischemia
Wound appearance: pale, necrotic base, minimal exudate
dressingOptions: Dry sterile dressing if non-viable tissue

dressingTypes.name: Dry Sterile Dressing (DSD)
dressingTypes.description: Standard gauze dressing providing protection. Changed when saturated or per order.

dressingTypes.name: Wet-to-Dry Dressing
dressingTypes.description: Moistened gauze placed in wound and allowed to dry. Mechanical debridement when removed. Painful — being replaced by more modern dressings.
indications: Wounds with necrotic tissue requiring mechanical debridement

dressingTypes.name: Hydrocolloid (DuoDERM)
dressingTypes.description: Adhesive dressing that creates moist wound healing environment. Contraindicated on infected wounds.

dressingTypes.name: Foam Dressing (Mepilex)
dressingTypes.description: Highly absorbent dressing. Atraumatic removal. Available in adhesive and non-adhesive forms.

dressingTypes.name: Calcium Alginate
dressingTypes.description: Highly absorbent fiber dressing derived from seaweed. Promotes hemostasis. Must have moisture to function.

dressingTypes.name: Silver Dressing (Mepilex Ag / Aquacel Ag)
dressingTypes.description: Antimicrobial dressing for infected or critically colonized wounds. Silver ions provide broad-spectrum activity.
indications: Prevention of infection in high-risk wounds

dressingTypes.name: Hydrogel
dressingTypes.description: Water-based gel that donates moisture to dry wounds. Promotes autolytic debridement.

dressingTypes.name: Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (VAC)
dressingTypes.description: Wound VAC system applying sub-atmospheric pressure via foam interface to promote healing, reduce edema, remove exudate, and promote granulation.

dressingTypes.name: Transparent Film (Tegaderm)
dressingTypes.description: Thin adhesive dressing allowing wound visibility. Maintains moist environment. Not absorbent.
indications: Over other dressings as secondary layer

vacSettings.name: Standard Continuous
vacSettings.notes: Default setting for most wounds. 24-hour continuous negative pressure.
vacSettings.sealIntegrityCheck: Listen and feel for air leak around dressing edges and tubing connections.

vacSettings.name: Standard Intermittent
vacSettings.notes: Used for wounds that may benefit from cyclic pressure changes. May promote granulation.
vacSettings.sealIntegrityCheck: Alarm will sound during off-cycle — confirm this is expected.

vacSettings.name: Low Pressure Continuous
vacSettings.notes: Used for sensitive tissue, flaps, grafts, exposed vessels. Lower pressure reduces tissue trauma.
vacSettings.sealIntegrityCheck: May be harder to maintain seal — check q2h.

vacSettings.name: High Pressure Continuous
vacSettings.notes: Rarely used. May be ordered for specific indications.

sealIntegrityChecks: Listen for air hissing at dressing edges
Check all tubing connections — click and secure
Re-seal any loose edges with additional drape/tape
If alarm persists: check canister full, check tubing kinked, check dressing integrity
vacAssessment.frequencyOfChecks: q2h seal check minimum; dressing change per order (typically every 48–72h or per wound care protocol)
outputMonitoring: Note output color (serosanguinous normal; bright red = bleeding — notify provider)
Canister change when 75% full or per device guidelines
alarmResponse: Dressing integrity alarm: check for air leak at all dressing edges and connections
Canister full alarm: change canister using sterile technique
Tube blockage: check for kinks, clots; milk tubing gently
